en.title: Point Assignment and Global Price Floor
en.description: Given an array of item prices, execute queries of three columns in order. 1 x v: set the price of item x directly to v, which may lower it; 2 v r: set every price to max(price,v), where the third column r is an unused placeholder. Output the prices after all queries.
en.input: Input, in order, n, n initial prices, q, and q lines of three-integer queries. Full original ranges: 1≤n,q≤200000, 0≤initial prices and valid v≤1000000000, point index 1≤x≤n. The original text did not give a separate numeric bound for the third placeholder of type2; this site interprets it per the original Java int[][] as −2147483648..2147483647, ignores its value, and does not require it to equal the threshold. The standard input is an explicit arrangement of the original function parameters.
en.output: Output the n final prices in the original item order, separated by whitespace.
en.explanation: The 001 original example keeps 8 9 8. In 006 Sample0, the third item of the original output, 3, is wrong; with the original five queries it should be 1 2 4 4 3; the intermediate state after the global floor 3 should be 3 3 4 4 3, and later point assignments can lower values again. The four 11s of Sample1 are correct, but keeping 1 at the end of the original explanation is wrong; writing 1 or 11 in the third column of type2 does not affect the result. The full basis for the corrections is in the editorial.
hints: You only need to care about each item's last point assignment.
When scanning in reverse, the global threshold only affects items not yet determined.
The third placeholder field is neither an index nor a threshold.
